claim: Point differential forecasts each team's remaining games better than its record does, after the record is regressed toward .500 by the same held-out fit. Cooling off / heating up relative to the current pace is mostly regression to the mean and is not the claim.
remaining_games_rule: games that had not kicked off at generated_at; earlier games are in excluded_started_games

forecasts.baseline: regressed record: linear map from first-k win% to rest-of-season win%, fitted on 2006-2025 at the team's k
forecasts.point_diff: the same map from Pythagorean win% (PF^2.37 / (PF^2.37 + PA^2.37)); identical to predictions_2026_wk08.json
forecasts.market: team ratings from 2026 point spreads (recency half-life 4 weeks, ridge 2); a game's own line when nflverse has one, else the ratings; spread -> win probability by a logistic fitted on 2006-2025
forecasts.same_pace: reference only: current win% x remaining games
forecasts.coin_flip: reference only: half of remaining games

p_beats_baseline: P(actual rest-of-season wins > baseline_rest_wins), from a logistic on gap_wins (point_diff_rest_wins - baseline_rest_wins) fitted on held-out 2006-2025 forecasts at the same k

rules: 1. MAE: mean absolute error of rest-of-season wins over all 32 teams for baseline, point_diff and market (same_pace and coin_flip reported for reference). A forecast's rest wins = its rest win% x the listed remaining games actually played (the market: the sum of its per-game probabilities over games played). Ties count half. Point differential passes if its MAE is lower than the baseline's.

2. Hit rate on the 10 highlighted teams: a point_diff_above_baseline team is a hit if its actual rest wins are above baseline_rest_wins, a point_diff_below_baseline team if they are below. Reported with the expected hits (the sum of the P(beats baseline) calls) and 5 of 10 as chance.
